body.html:
Barkpark · Cloud · revenue architecture

Barkpark Estate — the agent-native successor to WHM/cPanel

one box → many client estates · every account agent-native on day one · one new architecture piece

An operator carves a dedicated Barkpark into isolated client accounts — each with its own domain, its own branded Studio, its own content, tasks, sites, and its own AI agents as first-class users. Not a cheaper cPanel. The premium, API-first product cPanel would have been if agents had existed when it was designed. Working name: Estate (negotiable).

20+
client accounts per €12 box
1
genuinely new architecture pieces
3
tiers unlocked by the quota pair
0
incumbent panels with agent-native accounts

WHM conquered hosting by turning every agency into a distribution channel. Estate runs the same play — with a product no panel can copy.

The shape

The operator plane already exists (Cloud dashboard: fleet, lifecycle, adopt/eject). The account boundary already exists (Workspace — hard tenant boundary, atomic create_workspace_with_owner/2). What's missing is the connective tissue: a domain walking in the front door and landing inside the right workspace, wearing the right brand.

A domain lights up — the whole flow

The client experience that sells this: point DNS, refresh, you're in. No cert menus, no tickets, no renewal cron. Caddy's on_demand_tls makes it one ask-endpoint away:

WHM concept → Barkpark primitive

WHM conceptBarkpark primitiveStatus
WHM (operator panel)Cloud dashboard / instance admin — fleet, lifecycle, adopt/ejectEXISTS
AccountWorkspace — hard tenant boundary; workspace + owner membership + project + dataset in one transactionEXISTS
cPanel (per-account UI)Studio scoped to the workspaceEXISTS (scoping); needs workspace-only login view
Account usersMemberships; users-as-principals seamSEAM MERGED (#1276)
Addon domainsdomain → workspace routing + automatic TLSTHE GAP
Packages (quota presets)Per-workspace quotasMISSING — shared with playground/Solo
Suspend / unsuspendWorkspace freezeMISSING (small)
Website hostingbp sites — create · deploy · env · domain · logs, co-locatedEXISTS
White-labelTheme system — one themes/*.json per lookEXISTS
Per-account backupsPer-workspace export/bundlePARTIAL — instance-level archive/resurrect exists
Gap 1 · Host-based tenancy
domains table + Host-header plug + Caddy ask endpoint. The only genuinely new architecture — everything downstream already keys off workspace.
Gap 2 · Quota + suspend
Operator-set packages and freeze/unfreeze. Build once → playground, Solo tier, and Estate all fall out of the same work.
Gap 3 · Account-grade Studio
Workspace-only login, per-workspace theme binding, per-workspace export. Polish, not architecture — the 'cPanel moment'.

Why this is premium, not cheap

The temptation is to price this as commodity hosting. Wrong frame. Estate sells to people who bill their clients for it — the premium lives in what each account contains, and no incumbent has any of it:

• Agents are users, not add-ons. Every account ships a claimable task queue, MCP registration via bp onramp, and Papers. The client's AI works inside their account on day one — the agency configures nothing.
• Provisioning in seconds, not tickets. One atomic transaction creates the account; one DNS record lights the domain.
• White-label by design. A theme file per client — each client gets a Studio wearing their brand, not Barkpark's.
• Own your data, even as a sub-account. Per-workspace export and the eject doctrine extend to accounts: a client can leave the agency with their content intact. Confidence is a premium feature.
• The whole client stack on one bill. CMS, task board, docs, and the client's website (bp sites) consolidated on one box.

The operator experience — target UX

client-c — ○ suspended (unpaid)

One server carries an agency's full book; the agency margins comfortably; Barkpark's cost is one machine — and every agency becomes a channel that onboards clients for us. Position on the ladder: playground (free) → Solo (~$12) → Supporter ($69) → Estate ($99+, reseller) → Private ($149+, tunnel-only) → BYO (orchestration fee).
